name: Libya
sources: GDP $28.90bn and population 4,445,239 (World Bank, NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990).

Inflation 8% is an estimate. The World Bank publishes no consumer price series for Libya covering 1990 and the Jamahiriya's own statistics were not released; contemporary IMF and EIU commentary put it in high single figures, with shortages rather than posted prices doing the work. Listed as unverified.
Interest rate 7.0% is the lending rate the World Bank does record for Libya in 1990 (FR.INR.LEND); the deposit rate was 5.5% (FR.INR.DPST). Both were set by decree, not by a market.
Military 4.8% of GDP. SIPRI carries no Libya series; this is the IISS Military Balance defence budget of roughly $1.4bn against the World Bank's GDP. Listed as unverified.

Gross fixed capital formation 13.87% of GDP (World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, 1990), split 0.11 state / 0.03 private — the Green Book abolished retail trade and wage labour in 1980 and almost nothing was left in private hands to invest.

Tax take 0.38 is state revenue as a share of GDP, essentially all of it oil rent taken directly by the National Oil Corporation rather than levied. No published tax series exists. Listed as unverified.
Debt 0.10 of GDP. Libya borrowed almost nothing: oil revenue was the budget, and it is not in the World Bank's debtor reporting system at all.
Oil 1.375 mbd of crude (EIA international series, 1990), up 19.6% on 1989 as Libya produced over its OPEC quota during the Gulf crisis.

System is Command: the 1969 revolution nationalised the banks, the 1978 Green Book abolished rent and the 1980 decrees abolished private retail. This is the most thoroughly state-run economy in the region.
Authoritarianism 0.93, just under Ba'athist Iraq. Gaddafi held no office, parties were a capital offence under Law 71 of 1972, and the Revolutionary Committees hanged students on campus.
Stability 58: high oil revenue per head and a dense security apparatus against the 1984 Bab al-Azizia raid, repeated army plots, and the humiliation in Chad in 1987.
Separatism 0.12 is Cyrenaica and the tribal balance — the Senussi east that the monarchy came from and that Gaddafi's Sirte-based coalition kept out.

Military strength 10 for the largest inventory in Africa: roughly 2,000 Soviet tanks and 500 combat aircraft for an army of 85,000. It is scored barely above Indonesia's 8 and below Egypt's 14 on purpose. At Ouadi Doum and Maaten al-Sarra in 1987 that inventory was routed by Toyota pickups, which is the model's judgement about what Libya could actually do with it.
